title: Reduced fine moduli of nonempty cornered framed McKay algebras are quiver varieties after the specified dimension-vector enlargement
author: Alastair Craw; Soren Gammelgaard; Adam Gyenge; Balazs Szendroi
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 099, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.099; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a suitable enlargement of a dimension vector by explicit inequalities on the affine McKay graph, then controls extensions across removed vertices using finite-type Cartan positivity. It combines dense-stratum resolution, recollement and polystable decompositions to prove surjectivity of a previously constructed closed immersion. The reduced-scheme qualification and enlargement are essential; ordinary cornering or variation of GIT alone does not prove the result.

source_check.note: Read the complete local dependency chain of Theorem6.9: Proposition5.3 dense-stratum resolution and its dimension reduction; Lemmas5.4-5.5 and Proposition6.1 closed immersion; Lemma6.4 explicit dominating vector construction; Corollary6.5; Lemma6.8 recollement/polystable extension and Cartan bound; and the final closed-point surjectivity proof. Nakajima strata, ordinary GIT, earlier arbitrary-vector Hilbert/quiver correspondence and finite-dimensional recollement extension are identified cited background. The author expressly states the earlier extension proofs do not depend on the dimension vector; no new proof is substituted. Only the reduced cornered-moduli identification is selected, not the elementary framed Quot equivalence or downstream singularity variants. The repeated final definition of K contains a union typo; the same paragraph and Lemma6.8 define K as the complement, and source text is retained. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem6.9 for finite Gamma subset SL(2,C), nonempty I subset {0,...,r}, n_I in N^I and v matching n_i on I with M_thetaI(1,v) nonempty. A=Pi/(b*) for the framed McKay preprojective algebra, A_I=e_I A e_I, eta_I and theta_I exactly (4.2)/(5.1). Enlarge to v_prime in V(n_I) by Corollary6.5 and choose v_tilde_prime by Proposition5.3. The displayed closed immersion M_thetaI(1,v_prime)->M_AI(1,n_I) is an isomorphism of underlying reduced schemes, with the stated commutative resolution diagram. No assertion that the fine moduli scheme itself is reduced is added.
retained_original_metadata.editorial_warning: Original proof page19 repeats K={0,...,r} union I when naming vertex simples after explicitly defining K={0,...,r} minus I in the same paragraph. The preceding explicit definition and Lemma6.8 determine the complement scope. Preserve original source; no edited author formula is inserted.
